text:
Packaging notes from this week, plus what I found in the telemetry file.

On packaging, the Velopack step now builds the delta against the previous release rather than against the last successful build. That change is in build/pack.ps1 and it adds about 40 seconds per run, which is fine.

The awkward part is that the delta holds up while the previous nupkg is still on disk, and the CI cache evicts it after seven days. When the cache misses we fall back to a full package silently, so a release that looks like a 4 MB delta can quietly be a 96 MB download.

On telemetry, nothing leaves the machine. The counters live in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Scribe\usage.json and the tray menu has a Clear usage data item that deletes the file.

What I want to add is a rolling seven day window so the file stops growing, and a version stamp on the schema so a future reader knows which shape it is looking at. Neither is written yet.

text:
Why the overlay is a separate process, written down before someone tries to merge them again.

The tray shell is WPF and the overlay is WinUI 3. A WPF window with WS_EX_NOACTIVATE cannot host a Composition island without taking focus on the first paint, and taking focus is the one thing a dictation overlay can never do, because the keystroke it steals is the one the user is holding down.

Merging them would mean giving up either the island or the focus behaviour, and both of those are visible to the user on every single capture.

The cost of the split is the pipe. Every level update crosses a process boundary, which is 60 messages a second while a capture runs, and each one is a small allocation on both sides.

We measured that at 1.2 percent of a core on the Surface, which is the number to beat if anyone proposes a shared memory ring instead. The pipe code is in src/Scribe.Core/Ipc/OverlayChannel.cs and it is the smallest part of this whole design.

text:
What happened, and what we changed afterwards.

The update feed went stale on 3 August. The pack job published the installer to blob storage, and the feed json was written by a second step that had been failing quietly since 28 July, so every client kept seeing 2.0.7 as the newest release.

Nobody noticed for six days because the failure was a non zero exit code in a step marked continue-on-error: true. The workflow was green the whole time, and the signal we had was a drop in update checks that nobody was watching.

The changes are in .github/workflows/release.yml. The continue-on-error flag is gone from the publish step, and the job now reads the feed back and compares the version it finds with the tag it just built.

There is still no alert on that read back. That is the piece we must add before the next release, and until it exists a silent feed is something we would hear about from a user again.
note: A postmortem with two earned sections, two dates that must not drift, a YAML flag in code, and one must in the closing paragraph.

text: Autocorrect is why every identifier gets code formatting.
